What YEW does

Connect once. Access everything.

One connection gives your AI agent all 36 Robinhood Chain projects: trade, lend, borrow, use vaults and launch tokens, from a wallet on your computer.

01

Connect once

Install YEW and add one MCP connection to Claude Code, Codex, Cursor or another host. A wallet is created on your computer on first use.

02

Reach all 36 projects

Swap and place limit orders, lend and borrow, deposit into vaults, bridge, and launch and trade tokens on Pons, all in your own words.

03

Approve in chat

Your agent shows a plain summary and asks for a yes or no in chat before local signing. Approvals match the exact amount, never unlimited. Common actions take two steps: prepare, then execute.

Getting started

From install to your first prompt.

1. Install

Node.js 22.12.0 or newer. In your terminal:

npm install -g @yewagentkit/addon

The add-on includes @yewagentkit/core. YEW has had no subscription on Robinhood Chain since version 0.3.0, with approval in chat, an optional daily spending limit in USD, yew connect, Upoch reads. Agent 1's public tracker is being prepared. Version 0.3.12 is the current release; run yew --version to see the version you have.

2. Connect your agent

Connect directly with Node.js 22.12.0 or newer and npm on your PATH. These shortcuts run npx -y @yewagentkit/addon@0.3.12 mcp; no global YEW install is needed.

Add to Cursor Install in VS Code

For Claude Code, run these two commands inside Claude:

/plugin marketplace add YewAgentKit/yew
/plugin install yew@yew-agent-kit

Approve your app's install prompt and start a fresh session. If you already added YEW manually, use that connection or remove the duplicate before installing. Registering your agent ID still needs its own yes.

Claude Code, in your terminal:

yew connect claude

Codex, in your terminal:

yew connect codex

Cursor, in your project folder's terminal:

yew connect cursor

Gemini, Grok and other MCP hosts: Set up has each one. Start a fresh session after connecting.

3. Ask your agent

Paste a first prompt:

What can you do with YEW? Group the tools by project.
Show my YEW wallet address and balances. Do not send anything.
Quote a swap of 5 USDG to ETH with the best route. Show the preview and do not swap yet.
Lend 10 USDG on Priors. Show me the preview before anything is signed.
Deposit 10 USDG into a Steakhouse vault. Show me the preview first.
Show my open positions across every project.

Every action shows a summary first, then asks for your yes or no in chat.

One click selects a whole command or prompt. Then copy it: Cmd or Ctrl + C, or long-press on a phone.

For builders

One MCP for the whole chain.

MCP (Model Context Protocol) is a connection for AI tools. One local connection gives your agent 36 projects and 776 tools on Robinhood Chain: project information, balances, swaps, bridges, lending and identity.

Your agent's tool list shows the everyday tools. For anything not listed, it calls find_tool with what it wants to do, then run_tool with the tool's name and arguments. Tools run this way get the same checks, local guard, summary and yes-or-no approval as a direct call.

Connect Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, Cursor or another compatible host. Build your own workflows and experiment with autonomous agents. Pons token launches and curve buys are one example among the project tools.

In plain English

One connection. More things to ask.

An AI agent is an assistant that uses tools. YEW connects it to apps on Robinhood Chain, so you can ask it to check balances, compare a swap or use a project without wiring up each app yourself.

The tree is YEW. Its roots are the tools. The little houses are the projects your assistant can reach.

Your agent shows a plain summary of each action and asks for your yes or no in chat. After a yes, your wallet signs on your computer. A summary shows expected changes; actual outcomes can differ.

What it costs

No subscription. Every fee shown before you say yes.

Install YEW, connect your agent and use every tool. YEW has no subscription; reads, quotes and previews are free. YEW takes a 0.25% fee on swaps and bridges (including direct Uniswap swaps and official stock-token swaps; no YEW fee on FOBO, Pons and Hookr trades), plain sends (added on top) and Morpho bundle actions, plus an opt-in 10% Clanker creator-reward share and partner referral fees. Every fee is shown in the summary before you say yes. Network fees and each project's own fees still apply.

25% of YEW's income buys back and burns $YEW. Holding $YEW has no access perks.

01 · Your computer

A wallet that stays with you. It is created automatically on first use. Your private key never leaves your computer; YEW cannot recover a lost key. Recovery and export belong in your own terminal, never through the agent.

02 · The YEW server

Unsigned, until your wallet signs. The server never sees your key and never signs or sends a transaction. Your agent shows a plain summary and asks for a yes or no in chat, then your wallet signs on your computer. Common actions take two steps: prepare, then execute. You can set a daily spending limit, and change it by asking.

03 · Robinhood Chain

Straight to the project. Your swaps and deposits go straight from your wallet to the project. Simulation excludes gas and cannot prove off-chain settlement.

One MCP for the whole chain.

36 ecosystem projects share one local wallet. Docs, examples and contracts are MIT. The compiled npm packages are Free-to-Use, No Copying; their source and the hosted YEW service are private.

Ready your agent.

Connect your agent; the wallet is automatic. On a fresh install your agent asks one question about a daily spending limit, and you can skip it. Add a little ETH for network fees, then approve a public agent ID (ERC-8004) once. YEW previews and simulates transactions before local signing. Signature-only typed-data actions are shown for confirmation without transaction simulation. Its local guard refuses unexpected token movements or approvals before transaction signing. By default you approve each transaction and signature-only action with a yes or no in chat. YEW sets no spending caps or allowlists and does not judge whether a trade is wise. You can ask for a daily spending limit of your own and change it any time by asking.

02 · How YEW is funded

A small fee, and partner referral fees. YEW takes a 0.25% fee on swaps and bridges (including direct Uniswap swaps and official stock-token swaps via Priors, KyberSwap swaps, Velora swaps, and Relay bridges and swaps; there is no YEW fee on FOBO, Pons and Hookr trades), a 0.25% fee on plain sends (added on top so the recipient gets the full amount; dust under 400 base units and sends to or from the YEW treasury carry none), and a 0.25% fee on the loan amount in Morpho bundle actions (collateral-only steps and ordinary Morpho actions carry none). Clanker token launches offer an opt-in 10% Clanker creator-reward share (off unless chosen), and partners pay YEW referral fees when you use them through YEW. Every fee is shown in the summary before you say yes.

Partner referral fees. Borro is an official YEW partner. Borro's own team runs its product and contracts; YEW didn't build them and doesn't run them. Borro keeps 10% of the interest as its fee. On deposits using YEW's code, Borro pays YEW all of that fee for the first 12 months, then half. Borro pays monthly in USDG.

On hood.ag, YEW receives 5% of a name registration price and 4% of a resale price, and you get 5% or 4% off. A purchase with no referral says so in the summary.

03 · Income

25% buys back and burns $YEW. 25% of YEW's income buys back and burns $YEW. Holding $YEW has no access perks: its one link to YEW is the burns.

What you still pay.

Network fees go to the chain, not to YEW. Project fees go to the project. YEW's own fee is 0.25% on swaps and bridges (including direct Uniswap swaps and official stock-token swaps; no YEW fee on FOBO, Pons and Hookr trades), 0.25% added on top of plain sends, 0.25% on the loan amount in Morpho bundle actions, and an opt-in 10% creator-reward share on Clanker launches, and every fee appears in the summary before you say yes.

USDG is a dollar-denominated token. YEW makes no promises about token prices or investment outcomes.

Before you start

Install, connect and ask.

1. Install YEW

Use Node.js 22.12.0 or newer. In your terminal:

npm install -g @yewagentkit/addon

The add-on includes the core package. Check yew --version before funding or using actions.

Prefer to ask your agent? Copy this prompt

Set up YEW for this AI agent using Node.js 22.12.0 or newer. Install @yewagentkit/addon and connect the local MCP command yew mcp. Call account and tell me the public wallet address and network. If the wallet needs it, ask me to fund a little ETH for network fees, then re-check balances. Do not run yew init or yew export, read wallet/key files, or ask for keys or recovery words. Explain public agent ID registration and its cost; get my yes before registering.

2. Connect your assistant

Choose your client and run its command in your terminal after installing YEW. MCP is a connection for AI tools; YEW configures the local yew mcp command.

These connect Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI and Grok respectively. Claude Code must be installed. Cursor connects the current project, so run its command from that project's folder. The others connect your user account by default. Restart your app afterward. If YEW finds a conflicting entry, it explains how to fix it without overwriting it.

Claude Code
yew connect claude
Codex
yew connect codex
Cursor
yew connect cursor
Gemini
yew connect gemini
Grok
yew connect grok

3. Your wallet is automatic

Ask your agent: "What is my YEW wallet address?" YEW creates the wallet on first use. Check the address and that the network is Robinhood Chain. Your private key stays on your computer. Never give it or a recovery phrase to an agent. YEW cannot recover a lost key. For backup guidance, run yew backup in your own terminal; run yew export only in your own terminal, never through the agent, and keep the exported key offline.

Ask your agent:

Call account. Show only my public wallet address and network. Do not send a transaction.

You can also display the local public address in your terminal:

yew address

Your private key never leaves your computer. YEW cannot recover a lost key. Backups are optional: yew backup gives guidance. Run yew init or yew export only in your own terminal, never through the agent. Never paste a key or recovery words into chat.

4. Fund the wallet

Send a little ETH on Robinhood Chain for network fees, plus the money you want to use: ETH or USDG. Then ask your agent to check your balance.

If your money is on Base, your agent can prepare a Relay bridge to this wallet on Robinhood Chain. You can review the amount and fees before saying yes.

Base bridge-in uses the default RPC; you do not need to set one up. Ask the agent to check your balance after funding.

Use the network your wallet reports: Robinhood Chain mainnet is 4663. Then ask:

Re-check balances and show the ETH and USDG amounts on my selected network. Do not register or send a transaction yet.

Agent identity and approval in chat. Ask what you want to do. Reads work without an agent ID. For actions, YEW can prepare a public ERC-8004 agent ID registration after funding. The agent shows the public profile and network fee, then waits for your one approval before registration. You can instead link an existing ID; if another wallet owns it, its owner signs in their own terminal.

The agent asks once whether you want an optional daily spending limit in USD. Skipping leaves no limit; you can set or change it later in chat.

For an action, the agent calls a listed action tool or yew_prepare with {"name":"<tool>","arguments":{...}}. YEW builds and simulates it without signing, returning a summary, actionId and UTC expiry. The agent shows the summary and waits for your yes or no. After a yes, it calls yew_execute {"actionId":"<actionId>"}. YEW checks the action again and signs locally. Review the amounts, fees, permissions and warnings before deciding.

Explain yew_setup registration or linking and its cost. Show the public profile and network fee, then ask for my approval before registering.

Review the summary before saying yes or no in chat. You can ask to change the optional daily spending limit later.

5. Make your first request

Start with a read:

Call account, balances and positions. Show my network, balances and setup status in plain English. Do not send any transactions.

Then try a quote, without sending a transaction:

Find USDG and ETH with find_token. Quote 10 USDG (10000000 base units) to ETH with slippageBps 50. Explain the expected and minimum output. Do not swap.

More first prompts to paste:

What can you do with YEW? Group the tools by project.
Show my YEW wallet address and balances. Do not send anything.
Quote a swap of 5 USDG to ETH with the best route. Show the preview and do not swap yet.
Lend 10 USDG on Priors. Show me the preview before anything is signed.
Deposit 10 USDG into a Steakhouse vault. Show me the preview first.
Show my open positions across every project.

One click selects a whole command or prompt. Then copy it: Cmd or Ctrl + C, or long-press on a phone.

For a later action, inspect the preview and say yes or no in chat. After a yes, yew_execute checks the action again before local signing. Built approvals are exact. Simulations exclude gas and cannot prove external settlement or whether a token can later be sold.

Agents

YEW's agents

Every position. Every thesis. Wins and losses, on-chain.

Amounts vary and can be zero. Holders have no claim on an agent's money. Stock tokens can fall. Stock tokens are not available everywhere.

Agent 1's public tracker is being prepared. When it opens, the list of agents will be read here from YEW's server.

How to read this

Click a card to open it, or press Enter. Anything that was not measured says not measured (or Unknown in a full record), never zero. While this page is open, each card checks for a newer read every 5 minutes.

The cards. Each card is read from YEW's server in your browser. Closed, it shows the agent, what it does, one line on where it stands and a few figures. Open, it has a tab for what the agent did, a tab for what it holds and a tab for what it paid out. To close it, click the card again, press Escape or use the Close card button at its foot. A stock agent's card lists its moves, newest first, each with its reason and whether that reason was stamped before the result. A farm agent's card lists its harvests, and opens further to its full record.

Positions, theses and results. In a full record, follow each position from its thesis to its result. Wins and losses both. Every open position shows its value, its cost, its P/L and its thesis. Closed positions show what was realized. P/L is value now plus withdrawals minus deposits, with gas and fees counted. Income is counted separately from deposits. Unknown costs, gas or fees can leave the net P/L unknown, and anything the tracker cannot read is shown as Unknown or not measured, never as zero. The tracker's coverage gaps are listed in every open card.

Check a thesis yourself. Each thesis is stamped on-chain as a metadata entry on its agent's ERC-8004 ID, the number in the agent's open card. The chain holds only the hash. Take the thesis text exactly as shown, with no added line break, and compute its keccak256 hash over the UTF-8 bytes. It must equal the hash shown. Then open the stamp transaction and confirm that it wrote the same hash under the metadata key shown, on that agent's ID.

A thesis marked Written after entry was stamped after the position was already open. A thesis marked Written before entry was stamped with the trade or earlier. YEW does not edit a thesis once it is stamped.

YEW's tracker is a record of what each agent did. It is not advice, a forecast or a promise.

Follow the trail

Roadmap

Direction, not delivery dates. Priorities may change with testing and feedback.

01 · Done — On the Trail (Shipped)

  • One installable MCP, public docs and website.
  • Tools across Robinhood Chain projects behind one local wallet.
  • No subscription, with chat approvals and an optional daily spending limit.

02 · No Subscription and Burn Flywheel

  • No subscription: funded by swap, bridge, send and Morpho bundle fees, plus partner referral fees.
  • Use fee income to buy back and burn $YEW on Robinhood Chain.
  • Test every release against live market prices before it ships.

03 · Wider Reach

  • Pursue eligible MCP registry and official platform listings.
  • Share practical demos, tutorials and product updates.
  • Build working relationships with ecosystem teams.

04 · YEW's Own Agents

  • Launch YEW's own agents, funded by YEW's income and using YEW's tools on Robinhood Chain.
  • Route the results of YEW's agents into additional $YEW buybacks and burns.
  • Expand examples, project recipes and integration guides for builders.

05 · The Frontier

  • Explore later ideas such as agent access and cross-project workflows.
  • Research tools that connect useful workflows across Robinhood Chain projects.
  • Test automated strategies within defined spending limits and chat approvals.

Partnerships

Active partnerships

Projects, tools and data for AI agents on Robinhood Chain.

HEY Research Lab

Inside YEW, an agent can ask HEY Research Lab about a token or a project when the user asks, to see whether its team is still shipping, with sources. HEY Research Lab is an official YEW partner. HEY Research Lab's own team runs its product and contracts; YEW didn't build them and doesn't run them.

See HEY Research Lab's tools in Docs · Visit HEY Research Lab ↗

Borro

Inside YEW, an agent can lend USDG and official stock tokens into a Borro vault on Robinhood Chain. On deposits made with YEW's code, Borro pays YEW a share of the fee it keeps. A deposit into a vault without that code goes straight to the vault, and the summary says so. Borro is an official YEW partner. Borro's own team runs its product and contracts; YEW didn't build them and doesn't run them.

See Borro's tools in Docs

Factor

Inside YEW, an agent with a plain wallet can sign up as a Factor agent on Robinhood Chain, browse open jobs, apply to fixed-price jobs, draw an advance and deliver work. At most half of a job's price can be advanced before delivery. Factor is an official YEW partner. Factor's own team runs its product and contracts; YEW didn't build them and doesn't run them.

See Factor's tools in Docs

Raeto

Inside YEW, an agent can buy Raeto spending credit with USDG on Robinhood Chain, then use AI models, web search and page reading with one balance. YEW stops it at the limits you set. Raeto credit is for spending. You cannot turn it back into USDG. YEW integrates with Raeto. Raeto's own team runs its product and contracts; YEW didn't build them and doesn't run them.

FOBO coins on YEW

FOBO is a coin launchpad on Robinhood Chain. With YEW, your agent can browse and search coins, read a coin's details, check a portfolio and the leaderboard, buy and sell, launch a coin, place and cancel limit orders, and claim creator, referral and vesting payouts.

YEW asks before anything is signed. Your agent prepares the action and shows a plain summary in chat. Nothing is signed until you say yes. YEW checks every answer from FOBO against that summary first and refuses if anything differs, and a token approval is always for the exact amount, never unlimited.

Fees in plain words

  • FOBO charges a 2.5% tax on each trade after a coin's first minute. Of that, 1.5% goes to the coin's price floor, 0.6% to its creator and 0.4% to FOBO.
  • In a new coin's first minute the tax starts at 90% and falls to 2.5%. YEW's summary shows the tax at that moment before you say yes.
  • FOBO coins trade through FOBO's own pools, and YEW charges no fee on them. YEW's 0.25% swap fee applies to other swaps through Uniswap (including official stock-token swaps), KyberSwap or Velora.
  • Network fees apply to every transaction.

Coins launched on FOBO can lose value. Nothing here is advice or a promise.

About

YEW Agent Kit

YEW Agent Kit is independent software that connects an AI agent you already use to projects on Robinhood Chain, through tools on your own computer. One connection gives your agent the whole chain: trade, lend, borrow, use vaults and launch tokens, from a wallet on your computer.

The name is the story. Robin Hood's longbow was carved from yew — the tree that bends and does not break. YEW is built the same way: one strong connection, rooted in Sherwood, reaching every project on the chain.

YEW is independent software, not affiliated with Robinhood. It makes no promises about token prices or investment outcomes.

Privacy

Your keys stay yours.

This website is a static page. It does not ask you to connect a wallet, and a website visit does not connect one.

YEW runs on your computer. Your wallet is created locally on first use, and your private key never leaves your computer. YEW cannot recover a lost key, and no agent should ever be given a key or recovery words.

When your agent acts, the YEW server prepares unsigned work only: it never sees your key and never signs or sends a transaction. Your wallet signs on your computer, after your yes in chat.

Questions about privacy: DM @YewAgentKit on X.
